issues.legal_issue: A decree made before rent-control legislation was extended to a cantonment is saved when it was made by applying that legislation as if it were already in force.
material_facts: A landlord obtained a compromise decree under state rent-control legislation for possession of premises in a cantonment before that legislation had been formally extended to the cantonment.
The legislation was subsequently extended to the cantonment, and the tenant challenged whether the later amendment saved the earlier decree.
issues.conclusion: The decree was saved by the amended law, whether or not the extension of the rent-control legislation was retrospective.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(4) of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957, as amended by the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Amendment Act, 1972, saves qualifying decrees and orders made before the extension of state rent-control legislation to a cantonment. Its application is not confined to extensions made retrospectively under section 3(2). The statutory scheme addressed the effect of the rule in Indu Bhushan Bose v. Rama Sundari Devi, which held that Parliament had exclusive competence over regulation of house accommodation in cantonments.

predicates.pre_extension_rent_control_decree: A court made a decree regulating or ordering eviction from housing before rent-control legislation was extended to the area.
predicates.decree_applied_state_rent_law_as_if_in_f: The court made the decree by applying state rent-control legislation as though it were already in force in that area.
predicates.later_extension_to_cantonment: The state rent-control legislation was later extended to the cantonment.

issues.definition: When a court made a housing decree before rent-control legislation was extended to a cantonment by applying that legislation as if it were in force, and the legislation was later extended there, the decree is saved.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier ruling that a decree is a nullity does not bar a later execution proceeding when the ruling rested on a jurisdictional defect that subsequent legislation removes and validates.
material_facts: An executing court previously refused to execute a decree, holding it a nullity because state rent-control legislation did not apply to buildings in the cantonment.
Subsequent legislation removed that defect and validated decrees made by applying the state rent-control law to the cantonment.
The landlords later sought execution, and the tenant argued that the earlier ruling barred it as res judicata.
issues.conclusion: The earlier decision did not operate as res judicata and did not bar execution of the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mathura Prasad Bajoo Jaiswal v. Dessibai N. B. Jeejeebhoy, an erroneous determination of a question concerning the court's jurisdiction does not operate as res judicata when later proceedings are affected by a change in the law. Treating the earlier ruling as binding after legislation removes the jurisdictional defect and validates the decree would create a special rule of jurisdiction for the parties contrary to the law declared by the legislature. Section 3(4) of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957, as amended by the 1972 Act, supplied the relevant validation.

predicates.execution_proceeding: A party seeks to execute a decree in a later execution proceeding.
predicates.prior_ruling_decree_was_nullity_for_lack: A court previously held the decree a nullity because it considered the governing law inapplicable and therefore refused to exercise jurisdiction.
predicates.later_law_removes_defect_and_validates_d: A later change in law removes the defect underlying the prior ruling and validates the decree.

issues.definition: When a party later seeks execution of a decree previously held a nullity for lack of jurisdiction, a later law that removes that defect and validates the decree means the prior ruling does not bar execution as res judicata.
